title: Recover the Euclidean weak-FP simultaneous f-divergence dissipation join
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), Theorem 8.3.1 proof on PDF p. 219 (PDF page 230): after differentiating D_f(mu_t||nu_t), the adjoint evolution is moved onto observables and the diffusion/carre-du-champ chain rule yields the dissipation. This cell is the Euclidean/common-diffusion weak-FP realization of that mechanism, not the full abstract theorem statement.
target_statement: Clean-port the historical SimultaneousFDivergenceDissipation artifact onto the current Chapter 8 route. Assuming a dominated time derivative and explicit weak common-diffusion Fokker--Planck integration-by-parts identities for the p- and q-terms, combine the canonical spatial cancellation to prove D_f' = -diffusionScale * integral q f''(p/q) ||grad(p/q)||^2.

shared_floor_audit.notes: The historical dissipation join is a stronger existing repository artifact and is recovered rather than regenerated. Its old full gate was blocked upstream by the then-broken spatial-gradient parent. On current Lean 4.33, the recovered standalone spatial-pairing and dissipation-integrand definitions additionally needed CompleteSpace E because Mathlib's total gradient uses the Riesz representation; this is an interface repair at the definitions that actually use gradient, not a new source assumption on the final theorem. The full Chewi 8.3.1 statement is abstract in L_t, L_t^*, and Gamma_t and remains a later cell; this Euclidean weak-FP realization must not be presented as that full theorem.
